s1.syndrome_frame: Acute kidney injury with proteinuria and hematuria in a patient with a left ventricular assist device
salient_findings: Increased serum creatinine from 124 μmol/L to 354 μmol/L over two months
Urinary protein excretion of 2.2 g/day with microhaematuria
Positive blood cultures for Corynebacterium jeikeium
key_facts: 55-year-old man with severe dilated cardiomyopathy
Left ventricular assist device (LVAD; HeartMate II) implanted four years previously
Admitted for evaluation of low-grade fever
Serum creatinine increased from 124 μmol/L to 354 μmol/L over two months
Urinary protein excretion of 2.2 g/day
Microhaematuria without dysmorphic erythrocytes or casts
Elevated C-reactive protein and procalcitonin
Low serum complement C3 concentrations
Elevated PR3-ANCA and rheumatoid factor concentrations
Negative anti-MPO-ANCA
Multiple foci of increased metabolic activity at the LVAD driveline insertion site, the ventricular assist device pocket, and the LVAD outflow cannula on 18F-FDG PET-CT

differentials: Nephropathy associated with complement factor I deficiency
C3 glomerulonephritis associated with complement factor B deficiency
Renal amyloidosis associated with chronic infection
per_call: Nephropathy associated with complement factor I deficiency
C3 glomerulonephritis associated with complement factor B deficiency
Renal amyloidosis associated with chronic infection

shortlist.label: Post-infectious glomerulonephritis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a recent infection (Corynebacterium jeikeium) and renal biopsy shows features consistent with post-infectious glomerulonephritis

shortlist.label: Membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis
shortlist.why_kept: Renal biopsy shows increased mesangial matrix and mesangial cells, and immunohistology shows positive mesangial staining for IgM, C1q, and C3

shortlist.label: ANCA-associated vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has elevated PR3-ANCA and rheumatoid factor concentrations, and renal biopsy shows features consistent with vasculitis

shortlist.label: C3 glomerulopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Renal biopsy shows positive mesangial staining for C3 and electron microscopy shows mesangial regions with increased matrix and segmental subendothelial and mesangial osmiophilic deposits

shortlist.label: Device-related infection
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a left ventricular assist device and 18F-FDG PET-CT shows multiple foci of increased metabolic activity at the LVAD driveline insertion site, the ventricular assist device pocket, and the LVAD outflow cannula

raw.rationale: The patient has a left ventricular assist device (LVAD) and presents with low-grade fever, elevated C-reactive protein and procalcitonin, and multiple foci of increased metabolic activity at the LVAD driveline insertion site, the ventricular assist device pocket, and the LVAD outflow cannula on 18F-FDG PET-CT, which suggests a device-related infection. The renal biopsy findings of segmental sclerotic glomeruli, increased mesangial matrix and mesangial cells, and chronic tubulointerstitial damage are consistent with secondary effects of a systemic infection.

rejected.label: Post-infectious glomerulonephritis
rejected.why: The presence of Corynebacterium jeikeium in blood cultures and the clinical context suggest a device-related infection rather than a post-infectious glomerulonephritis.

rejected.label: Membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis
rejected.why: While the renal biopsy shows mesangial proliferation, the clinical context and the presence of device-related infection make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: ANCA-associated vasculitis
rejected.why: The patient has elevated PR3-ANCA, but the clinical context and the presence of device-related infection make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: C3 glomerulopathy
rejected.why: The patient has low serum complement C3 concentrations and positive mesangial staining for C3, but the clinical context and the presence of device-related infection make this diagnosis less likely.
